text:
Maya R: :rotating_light: incident-bot just fired a critical — surge in 429/503s from inference-prod (region-us-east). PD alert INC-2026.

incident-bot: PagerDuty -> Critical: 4xx/5xx spike on inference-prod (last 5m). Top anomaly: 503s up 7x, 429s up 4x. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/abcd/429-503-trends

Jordan L: seeing same. overall 429 rate ~6% but one tenant (TENANT-42) is at ~22% of its requests failing with 429, also many 503s from streaming workers.

Priya S: do we know if this correlates with any deploy? I can check deploy bot but nothing in last 30m on runtime.

Eli K: I pulled logs, looks like KV cache pressure and head-of-line blocking on streaming shards. A large concurrent batch from TENANT-42 started ~10:14 and kept growing.

Maya R: ok, immediate plan: 1) apply soft tenant-level rate cap for TENANT-42, 2) temporarily disable streaming for guest tier & fallback to non-streaming path, 3) scale up streaming pool by +2 nodes while we monitor. Priya, can you run the cap? Jordan, can you disable streaming for guest? Eli, kick off scale.

Priya S: on it. running admin patch now:
```
curl -X POST \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  https://admin.redwood.company/v1/tenants/TENANT-42/rate_limit \
  -d '{"max_rps": 10, "burst": 20, "reason": "live mitigation - 4xx/5xx spike"}'
```

Priya S: response 200, applied. will take effect across edge in ~30s.

Jordan L: disabling streaming for guest tier now via config toggle in console -> rollout. command:
```
redwoodctl config set --scope=guest --key=streaming.enabled --value=false --reason=mitigation
```

Jordan L: toggle submitted. grad rollout 50% -> 100% in 45s.

Eli K: scaled streaming pool by adding 2 nodes (g4dn.xlarge). k8s patch:
```
kubectl -n inference-prod scale deployment/streaming-service --replicas=12
```

Maya R: good. I'm opening a small dashboard view and watching the 3 main metrics: overall 429 rate, 503 rate, and per-tenant 429 breakdown.

incident-bot: Note: automated fallback policy triggered for model-llama-13b when streaming failed, fallback to non-streaming variant.

Jordan L: early signs: TENANT-42 429s dropped from 22% -> 9% after cap. overall 429s dipped to 4.1%. 503s are slower to move, currently 5.2%.

Priya S: recommended follow-ups: keep tenant cap in place for 30m, request TENANT-42 to throttle upstream or investigate their burst. Also open support ticket to inform them and offer options.

Eli K: 503s look tied to memory pressure on streaming pods; scaling helped a bit but some pods OOM-killed earlier. I'm increasing pod memory limit on streaming-service to reduce churn. patching now.

Jordan L: I think we should also reduce max_tokens default for guest/low-tier to 512 to lower per-request resource usage. Want me to flip that?

Maya R: yes, do it but do a gradual rollout: 25% -> 100% over 10m. Keep observability on request latencies.

Jordan L: set. command:
```
redwoodctl config set --scope=guest --key=max_tokens.default --value=512 --rollout=gradual:10m
```

Priya S: support ticket created to TENANT-42 (SUP-9913). Snippet sent: "We applied a temporary soft RPS cap and saw improvement; please check request patterns. If you need sustained high QPS, open an account-level plan to reserve capacity."

Maya R: oncall handoff in ~20m, @Jordan you will be primary for next shift. Document actions in postmortem. If any regression, escalate to infra lead.

Eli K: monitoring shows 503s falling to 2.8% now. Pod restarts down. Memory limit bump seems effective.

Maya R: green checks: TENANT-42 429s at 6%, overall 429s 2.6%, 503s 2.2%. Rolling back any temporary fix will wait until metrics stable for 15m.

incident-bot: Alert update -> severity reduced to "major".

Jordan L: I'll keep streaming disabled for guest for 30m and hold the tenant cap. If no regressions, we can unwind: remove tenant cap -> re-enable streaming -> revert token limits (in that order).

Priya S: I'll coordinate the customer comms and add recommended client-side backoff guidance.

Maya R: thanks team. quick retrospective notes to include: - root cause: large concurrent burst + insufficient streaming pod headroom - mitigations: tenant soft cap, disable streaming for low-tier, scale nodes, increase memory limits, reduce default max_tokens for low-tier - next steps: add auto-shedding for noisy tenants, surface per-tenant slow-start in console, task to add graceful streaming backpressure.

Eli K: adding a dashboard panel to show per-tenant QPS and 429% in one place. PR: https://git.redwood.company/infra/alerts/pulls/128

Maya R: handing off to @Jordan L. If anything spikes back up call the PD escalation. I'll be available on the thread for 10m then offline. :white_check_mark:

Jordan L: acknowledged. monitoring and oncall. I'll file the incident ticket in postmortems/ with links to dashboards and steps taken.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty INC-2026 acknowledged by Maya R.

Maya R: closing notes: keep tenant cap until TENANT-42 confirms they throttled. We'll reconvene after 30m to decide unwind. Good job everyone. :tada:
